text: Which of the following is $\text{NOT}$ a $\text{Characteristics}$ of $\text{Living}$ $\text{Organisms}$?
explanation: $\text{Locomotion}$ is the $\text{Movement}$ of an $\text{Organism}$ from $\text{One}$ $\text{Place}$ to $\text{Another}$. While all living organisms exhibit $\text{Movement}$ (internal or external), not all undergo $\text{Locomotion}$ (e.g., $\text{Sessile}$ $\text{Plants}$). All living things exhibit $\text{Respiration}$, $\text{Growth}$, $\text{Excretion}$, $\text{Irritability}$, $\text{Nutrition}$, and $\text{Reproduction}$.

text: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$ in $\text{Plants}$ is $\text{Mainly}$ $\text{Composed}$ of:
image: [Diagram of a plant cell highlighting the cell wall]
explanation: The $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$ is a $\text{Rigid}$ $\text{Layer}$ $\text{Lying}$ $\text{Outside}$ the $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$ and is $\text{Primarily}$ $\text{Made}$ of $\text{Cellulose}$, a $\text{Polysaccharide}$.

text: Which part of the $\text{Tooth}$ contains $\text{Nerves}$ and $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Vessels}$?
explanation: The $\text{Pulp}$ $\text{Cavity}$ is the $\text{Central}$ $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Tooth}$ that is $\text{Filled}$ with $\text{Connective}$ $\text{Tissue}$, $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Vessels}$, and $\text{Nerves}$, which $\text{Maintain}$ the $\text{Vitality}$ of the $\text{Tooth}$.

text: The $\text{Enzyme}$ $\text{Ptyalin}$ is $\text{Responsible}$ for the $\text{Digestion}$ of:
explanation: $\text{Ptyalin}$, also known as $\text{Salivary}$ $\text{Amylase}$, is an $\text{Enzyme}$ found in $\text{Saliva}$ that $\text{Begins}$ the $\text{Hydrolysis}$ of $\text{Starch}$ (a $\text{Carbohydrate}$) into simpler sugars.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Conversion}$ of $\text{Glucose}$ to $\text{Glycogen}$ in the $\text{Liver}$ is called:
explanation: $\text{Glycogenesis}$ is the $\text{Metabolic}$ $\text{Pathway}$ that $\text{Results}$ in the $\text{Formation}$ of $\text{Glycogen}$ from $\text{Glucose}$, primarily in the $\text{Liver}$ and $\text{Muscle}$ $\text{Tissues}$.

text: In $\text{Plants}$, $\text{Water}$ is $\text{Transported}$ from the $\text{Roots}$ to the $\text{Leaves}$ through the:
image: [Cross-section of a plant stem showing xylem and phloem]
explanation: $\text{Xylem}$ $\text{Vessels}$ are $\text{Specialized}$ $\text{Tissues}$ that $\text{Conduct}$ $\text{Water}$ and $\text{Dissolved}$ $\text{Mineral}$ $\text{Salts}$ $\text{Upwards}$ from the $\text{Roots}$ to the $\text{Rest}$ of the $\text{Plant}$.

text: The $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Food}$ $\text{Material}$ in the $\text{Phloem}$ is $\text{Referred}$ to as:
explanation: $\text{Translocation}$ is the $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Sugars}$ (mainly $\text{Sucrose}$) and $\text{Amino}$ $\text{Acids}$ from the $\text{Sites}$ of $\text{Production}$ ($	ext{Leaves}$) to the $\text{Sites}$ of $\text{Storage}$ or $\text{Use}$ ($	ext{Roots}$, $\text{Fruits}$), $\text{Occurring}$ in the $\text{Phloem}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Organs}$ $\text{Detoxifies}$ the $\text{Blood}$ and $\text{Breaks}$ $\text{Down}$ $\text{Old}$ $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$?
explanation: The $\text{Liver}$ plays a $\text{Major}$ $\text{Role}$ in $\text{Detoxification}$ of $\text{Harmful}$ $\text{Substances}$ in the $\text{Blood}$. It is also $\text{Involved}$ in $\text{Breaking}$ $\text{Down}$ $\text{Old}$ $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ and $\text{Converting}$ the $\text{Haemoglobin}$ into $\text{Bile}$ $\text{Pigments}$.

text: The $\text{Waste}$ $\text{Product}$ of $\text{Protein}$ $\text{Metabolism}$ in $\text{Mammals}$ that is $\text{Excreted}$ as $\text{Urine}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Excess}$ $\text{Amino}$ $\text{Acids}$ from $\text{Protein}$ $\text{Breakdown}$ are $\text{Deaminated}$ in the $\text{Liver}$, $\text{Forming}$ $\text{Ammonia}$, which is then $\text{Converted}$ to the $\text{Less}$ $\text{Toxic}$ $\text{Urea}$ in the $\text{Urea}$ $\text{Cycle}$. $\text{Urea}$ is the $\text{Main}$ $\text{Nitrogenous}$ $\text{Waste}$ $\text{Excreted}$ in $\text{Mammalian}$ $\text{Urine}$.

text: Which $\text{Layer}$ of the $\text{Skin}$ $\text{Contains}$ $\text{Fat}$ for $\text{Insulation}$ and $\text{Energy}$ $\text{Storage}$?
image: [Cross-section of the human skin showing layers]
explanation: The $\text{Subcutaneous}$ $\text{Layer}$ ($	ext{Hypodermis}$) $\text{Lies}$ $\text{Beneath}$ the $\text{Dermis}$ and is $\text{Rich}$ in $\text{Adipose}$ $\text{Tissue}$ ($	ext{Fat}$), $\text{Serving}$ as an $\text{Insulator}$ and a $\text{Major}$ $\text{Energy}$ $\text{Reserve}$.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Eye}$ that $\text{Controls}$ the $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Light}$ $\text{Entering}$ the $\text{Eye}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human eye highlighting the iris and pupil]
explanation: The $\text{Iris}$ is the $\text{Colored}$ $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Eye}$. It $\text{Contains}$ $\text{Muscles}$ that $\text{Contract}$ or $\text{Relax}$ to $\text{Adjust}$ the $\text{Size}$ of the $\text{Pupil}$, thereby $\text{Controlling}$ the $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Light}$ $\text{Reaching}$ the $\text{Retina}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Hormones}$ is $\text{Associated}$ with the $\text{Fight}$-or-$\text{Flight}$ $\text{Response}$?
explanation: $\text{Adrenaline}$ (Epinephrine) is $\text{Secreted}$ by the $\text{Adrenal}$ $\text{Glands}$ in $\text{Response}$ to $\text{Stress}$ or $\text{Danger}$. It $\text{Prepares}$ the $\text{Body}$ for $\text{Intense}$ $\text{Physical}$ $\text{Activity}$ ($	ext{Fight}$ or $\text{Flight}$).

text: The $\text{Growth}$ $\text{Movement}$ of a $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Part}$ in $\text{Response}$ to $\text{Water}$ is called:
explanation: $\text{Hydrotropism}$ is the $\text{Growth}$ or $\text{Turning}$ $\text{Movement}$ of a $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Part}$ in $\text{Response}$ to the $\text{Stimulus}$ of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Concentration}$ ($	ext{Hydro}$). $\text{Roots}$ typically show $\text{Positive}$ $\text{Hydrotropism}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Fusing}$ the $\text{Male}$ and $\text{Female}$ $\text{Gametes}$ in $\text{Sexual}$ $\text{Reproduction}$ is called:
explanation: $\text{Fertilization}$ is the $\text{Union}$ of the $\text{Male}$ $\text{Gamete}$ ($	ext{Sperm}$ or $\text{Pollen}$ $\text{Nucleus}$) and the $\text{Female}$ $\text{Gamete}$ ($	ext{Egg}$ $\text{Cell}$) to $\text{Form}$ a $\text{Zygote}$.

text: The $\text{Stage}$ of $\text{Development}$ in $\text{Insects}$ characterized by $\text{Major}$ $\text{Body}$ $\text{Reorganization}$ is the:
image: [Life cycle diagram of a butterfly showing the pupa stage]
explanation: In $\text{Insects}$ that $\text{Undergo}$ $\text{Complete}$ $\text{Metamorphosis}$ ($	ext{Holometabolism}$), the $\text{Pupa}$ $\text{Stage}$ is a $\text{Non}$-$\text{Feeding}$, $\text{Quiescent}$ $\text{Stage}$ where $\text{Tissues}$ are $\text{Broken}$ $\text{Down}$ and $\text{Reformed}$ into the $\text{Adult}$ $\text{Form}$.

text: The $\text{Inheritance}$ of $\text{Sex}$ in $\text{Humans}$ is $\text{Determined}$ by the $\text{Chromosome}$ $\text{Contributed}$ by the:
image: [Punnett square illustrating sex determination (XX x XY)]
explanation: Females have $\text{XX}$ sex chromosomes ($	ext{Contribute}$ $\text{X}$). $\text{Males}$ have $\text{XY}$ sex chromosomes ($	ext{Contribute}$ $\text{X}$ or $\text{Y}$). The $\text{Father's}$ $\text{Sperm}$ ($	ext{X}$ or $\text{Y}$) $\text{Determines}$ the $\text{Sex}$ of the $\text{Child}$ ($	ext{XX}$ = $\text{Female}$, $\text{XY}$ = $\text{Male}$).

text: If a $\text{Tall}$ $\text{Plant}$ ($	ext{TT}$) is $\text{Crossed}$ with a $\text{Dwarf}$ $\text{Plant}$ ($	ext{tt}$), the $\text{Genotype}$ of the $\text{F1}$ $\text{Generation}$ is:
explanation: A cross between $\text{TT}$ and $\text{tt}$ yields $\text{100\%}$ $\text{Tt}$ $\text{Genotype}$ in the $\text{F1}$ $\text{Generation}$. The $\text{Offspring}$ are all $\text{Heterozygous}$.

text: The $\text{Evolutionary}$ $\text{Theory}$ that states that $\text{Acquired}$ $\text{Characteristics}$ are $\text{Inherited}$ is $\text{Associated}$ with:
explanation: $\text{Lamarckism}$, or the $\text{Inheritance}$ of $\text{Acquired}$ $\text{Characteristics}$, was $\text{Proposed}$ by $\text{Jean}$-$\text{Baptiste}$ $\text{Lamarck}$. This $\text{Theory}$ is $\text{Now}$ $\text{Discredited}$ in $\text{Favor}$ of $\text{Darwin's}$ $\text{Natural}$ $\text{Selection}$.

text: The $\text{Absence}$ of a $\text{Nucleus}$ in $\text{Mature}$ $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ is an $\text{Adaptation}$ for:
explanation: The $\text{Lack}$ of a $\text{Nucleus}$ and $\text{Other}$ $\text{Organelles}$ $\text{Maximizes}$ the $\text{Internal}$ $\text{Space}$ $\text{Available}$ for $\text{Haemoglobin}$, thus $\text{Increasing}$ the $\text{Oxygen}$-$\text{Carrying}$ $\text{Capacity}$ of the $\text{Cell}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Diseases}$ is $\text{Caused}$ by a $\text{Fungus}$?
explanation: $\text{Ringworm}$ is a $\text{Common}$ $\text{Fungal}$ $\text{Infection}$ of the $\text{Skin}$ ($	ext{Tinea}$ $\text{Species}$). $\text{Malaria}$ is $\text{Protozoan}$, $\text{Tuberculosis}$ and $\text{Typhoid}$ are $\text{Bacterial}$.

text: The $\text{Habitat}$ $\text{Where}$ $\text{Annelids}$ ($	ext{Earthworms}$) are $\text{Most}$ $\text{Commonly}$ $\text{Found}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Earthworms}$ ($	ext{Annelids}$) $\text{Thrive}$ in $\text{Moist}$, $\text{Organic}$-$\text{Rich}$ $\text{Soil}$ ($	ext{Loam}$) as it $\text{Provides}$ $\text{Food}$ and $\text{Ease}$ of $\text{Movement}$.

text: The $\text{Tissues}$ $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Secondary}$ $\text{Growth}$ in $\text{Plants}$ is the:
image: [Cross-section of a dicot stem showing vascular and cork cambium]
explanation: $\text{Secondary}$ $\text{Growth}$ (increase in $\text{Girth}$) is $\text{Caused}$ by $\text{Activity}$ in the $\text{Lateral}$ $\text{Meristems}$, $\text{Specifically}$ the $\text{Vascular}$ $\text{Cambium}$ and $\text{Cork}$ $\text{Cambium}$.

text: In the $\text{Nitrogen}$ $\text{Cycle}$, the $\text{Conversion}$ of $\text{Atmospheric}$ $\text{Nitrogen}$ to $\text{Nitrates}$ is $\text{Achieved}$ by:
explanation: $\text{Nitrogen}$-$\text{Fixing}$ $\text{Bacteria}$ (e.g., $\text{Rhizobium}$) $\text{Convert}$ $\text{Atmospheric}$ $\text{Nitrogen}$ ($	ext{N}_2$) into $\text{Ammonia}$ ($	ext{NH}_3$). This is then $\text{Converted}$ to $\text{Nitrates}$ by $\text{Nitrifying}$ $\text{Bacteria}$ in a $\text{Subsequent}$ $\text{Stage}$ ($	ext{Nitrification}$). $\text{Nitrogen}$-$\text{fixing}$ $\text{Bacteria}$ is the $\text{Initial}$ $\text{Step}$ required to $\text{Bring}$ $\text{Atmospheric}$ $\text{Nitrogen}$ into a $\text{Form}$ usable by $\text{Plants}$.

text: The $\text{Instrument}$ $\text{Used}$ to $\text{Measure}$ $\text{Wind}$ $\text{Speed}$ is the:
explanation: An $\text{Anemometer}$ is a $\text{Device}$ $\text{Used}$ for $\text{Measuring}$ $\text{Wind}$ $\text{Speed}$ or the $\text{Velocity}$ of $\text{Gas}$ $\text{Flow}$.

text: In a $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$, $\text{Producers}$ are $\text{Organisms}$ that $\text{Feed}$ on:
explanation: $\text{Producers}$ ($	ext{Autotrophs}$), $\text{Mainly}$ $\text{Green}$ $\text{Plants}$, $\text{Manufacture}$ their $\text{Own}$ $\text{Food}$ $\text{Using}$ $\text{Energy}$ ($	ext{Sunlight}$) and $\text{Inorganic}$ $\text{Materials}$ ($	ext{Water}$ and $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ $\text{via}$ $\text{Photosynthesis}$).

text: Which of the following $\text{Organisms}$ $\text{Belongs}$ to the $\text{Phylum}$ $\text{Arthropoda}$?
explanation: The $\text{Phylum}$ $\text{Arthropoda}$ includes $\text{Insects}$, $\text{Spiders}$, $\text{Crustaceans}$, and $\text{Myriapods}$ ($	ext{Centipedes}$ and $\text{Millipedes}$). They are $\text{Characterized}$ by $\text{Jointed}$ $\text{Legs}$ and an $\text{Exoskeleton}$.

text: The $\text{Type}$ of $\text{Joint}$ found at the $\text{Hip}$ and $\text{Shoulder}$ is a:
explanation: A $\text{Ball}$-$\text{and}$-$\text{Socket}$ $\text{Joint}$ ($	ext{Hip}$ and $\text{Shoulder}$) $\text{Allows}$ for $\text{Movement}$ in $\text{Many}$ $\text{Planes}$ ($	ext{Rotation}$, $\text{Flexion}$, $\text{Extension}$, $\text{Abduction}$, $\text{Adduction}$).

text: The $\text{Major}$ $\text{Cause}$ of $\text{Desertification}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Desertification}$ is the $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Fertile}$ $\text{Land}$ $\text{Becoming}$ $\text{Desert}$, typically as a $\text{Result}$ of $\text{Drought}$, $\text{Deforestation}$, or $\text{Inappropriate}$ $\text{Agriculture}$ $\text{Practices}$ ($	ext{Overgrazing}$).

text: Which $\text{Gas}$ is $\text{Given}$ $\text{Off}$ when a $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Respires}$ in the $\text{Dark}$?
explanation: $\text{Respiration}$ $\text{Occurs}$ $\text{Continuously}$ ($	ext{Day}$ and $\text{Night}$) and $\text{Involves}$ the $\text{Uptake}$ of $\text{Oxygen}$ and the $\text{Release}$ of $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$. In the $\text{Dark}$, $\text{Photosynthesis}$ does $\text{Not}$ $\text{Occur}$, so only the $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ from $\text{Respiration}$ is $\text{Released}$.

text: The $\text{Organism}$ that $\text{Causes}$ $\text{Tuberculosis}$ ($	ext{TB}$) is a:
explanation: $\text{Tuberculosis}$ ($	ext{TB}$) is $\text{Caused}$ by the $\text{Bacterium}$ $\text{Mycobacterium}$ $\text{Tuberculosis}$.

text: The $\text{Specialized}$ $\text{Cells}$ in the $\text{Nervous}$ $\text{System}$ $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Transmitting}$ $\text{Impulses}$ are:

text: Which of the following $\text{Adaptations}$ $\text{Helps}$ a $\text{Desert}$ $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Reduce}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Loss}$?
explanation: A $\text{Thick}$ $\text{Waxy}$ $\text{Cuticle}$ $\text{Minimizes}$ $\text{Cuticular}$ $\text{Transpiration}$. $\text{Spines}$ ($	ext{Modified}$ $\text{Leaves}$) $\text{Reduce}$ the $\text{Surface}$ $\text{Area}$ for $\text{Transpiration}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Clotting}$ $\text{Requires}$ the $\text{Presence}$ of $\text{Which}$ $\text{Mineral}$ $\text{Ion}$?
explanation: $\text{Calcium}$ $\text{Ions}$ ($	ext{Ca}^{2+}$) are $\text{Essential}$ $\text{Co-factors}$ in the $\text{Cascade}$ of $\text{Enzymatic}$ $\text{Reactions}$ that $\text{Lead}$ to the $\text{Formation}$ of a $\text{Fibrin}$ $\text{Clot}$.

text: A $\text{Community}$ in $\text{Ecology}$ is $\text{Defined}$ as:
image: [Image illustrating a biological community with various species interacting]
explanation: An $\text{Ecology}$ $\text{Community}$ is the $\text{Assemblage}$ of $\text{All}$ $\text{Populations}$ ($	ext{Different}$ $\text{Species}$) $\text{Living}$ and $\text{Interacting}$ $\text{Within}$ a $\text{Given}$ $\text{Area}$ (i.e., the $\text{Biotic}$ $\text{Components}$). If the $\text{Physical}$ $\text{Environment}$ ($	ext{Abiotic}$ $\text{Factors}$) is $\text{Included}$, it is an $\text{Ecosystem}$.

explanation: In the $\text{Proximal}$ $\text{Convoluted}$ $\text{Tubule}$, $\text{Essential}$ $\text{Nutrients}$ like $\text{Glucose}$ and $\text{Amino}$ $\text{Acids}$ are $\text{Completely}$ $\text{Reabsorbed}$ back into the $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Stream}$ $\text{Against}$ a $\text{Concentration}$ $\text{Gradient}$ $\text{Via}$ $\text{Active}$ $\text{Transport}$.

text: The $\text{Smallest}$ $\text{Structural}$ and $\text{Functional}$ $\text{Unit}$ of the $\text{Nervous}$ $\text{System}$ is the:
explanation: The $\text{Neuron}$ ($	ext{Nerve}$ $\text{Cell}$) is the $\text{Basic}$ $\text{Unit}$ of the $\text{Nervous}$ $\text{System}$, $\text{Specialized}$ to $\text{Transmit}$ $\text{Information}$ ($	ext{Nerve}$ $\text{Impulses}$). explanation: $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cells}$ typically $\text{Have}$ a $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$ ($	ext{Absent}$ in $\text{Animal}$ $\text{Cells}$) and $\text{Chloroplasts}$ ($	ext{Required}$ for $\text{Photosynthesis}$, $\text{Absent}$ in $\text{Animal}$ $\text{Cells}$).

text: The $\text{Process}$ by which $\text{Oxygen}$ is $\text{Transported}$ from the $\text{Lungs}$ to the $\text{Body}$ $\text{Tissues}$ is $\text{Mainly}$ by:
explanation: Over $\text{98\%}$ of $\text{Oxygen}$ is $\text{Bound}$ to $\text{Haemoglobin}$ in $\text{Red}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ for $\text{Transport}$ from the $\text{Lungs}$ to the $\text{Body}$ $\text{Tissues}$.

text: The $\text{Most}$ $\text{Effective}$ $\text{Method}$ of $\text{Controlling}$ $\text{Malaria}$ $\text{in}$ an $\text{Area}$ is to:
explanation: $\text{Malaria}$ is $\text{Transmitted}$ by the $\text{Anopheles}$ $\text{Mosquito}$, which $\text{Breeds}$ in $\text{Stagnant}$ $\text{Water}$. $\text{Controlling}$ the $\text{Mosquito}$ $\text{Population}$ by $\text{Eliminating}$ $\text{Breeding}$ $\text{Sites}$ ($	ext{Drainage}$) is the $\text{Most}$ $\text{Effective}$ and $\text{Sustainable}$ $\text{Control}$ $\text{Measure}$.
